source: Figma MCP reads (get_metadata, get_design_context, get_variable_defs, get_screenshot) of the Core Component file.

use_when: To trigger a primary action, such as submitting a form or confirming a choice.
When the action is a single, clear next step the user should take.
For calls-to-action that need visual emphasis — use the filled/primary style.
For secondary or less prominent actions — use the outline style instead of a second filled button.
To open a modal, drawer, or another view, when the action is not a navigation link.
For destructive actions (e.g. delete, remove), paired with the error/danger state.
Inside forms, toolbars, cards, and dialogs — wherever a discrete, tappable action is needed.
dont_use_when: For navigation between pages or views — use a Link component instead.
When more than one primary action competes for attention on the same screen — keep only one primary button per view.
As a label or static status indicator — use a Badge/Lozenge component instead.
For a toggleable on/off state — use a Toggle or Checkbox component instead.
best_practice: Use clear, action-oriented labels (e.g. "Save changes", not "OK").
Keep a single primary (filled) button per screen or section; make all other actions secondary/outline.
Always design a hover and error/disabled state so users get feedback on interaction.
Don't stack more than two buttons side by side without a clear visual hierarchy.
Keep button labels to 1–3 words; avoid full sentences.
Reserve the error/outline-error state for destructive or blocking actions only.
Keep a minimum 40px tap target height for touch interfaces.

variantMatrix.note: The documentation frame lays out state (rows) against StartIcon: True / False (columns), once with EndIcon: True and once with EndIcon: False.

themes.note: The Button page renders every cell in one theme. There is no dark-mode frame on the page.

Avatar.description: Shows a person's profile photo in a circle. size: sm 24px (default; dense lists, inline with text), md 30px (the header avatar), lg 40px (profiles, message threads). Drop the photo onto the photo layer; it fills and crops to the circle.

variantMatrix.note: The documentation frame lays the three sizes out in one row, sm 24x24, md 30x30 and lg 40x40, each labelled.

themes.note: The Avatar frame renders every size once, on the dark overlay background (--color-bg-overlay). It has no separate light and dark frames.

use_when: To show the signed-in user's profile photo, such as in the header.
To represent a person (a host, guest or reviewer) next to their name or content.
Use md (30px) in the header, sm (24px) in dense lists or inline with text, and lg (40px) where the person is the focus, such as a profile or message thread.
dont_use_when: For brand or company logos: use the Logo component instead.
For listing or content photos: use the Image component instead.
As a clickable control on its own: place it inside a Button or Link so it has an accessible name.
best_practice: Crop photos square with the face centred; the circle clips the corners.
Keep one avatar size within the same list or row.
Give the image alt text with the person's name, or leave it empty when the name is shown right beside it.
Use only the sm, md and lg sizes; don't scale an avatar to other sizes.
Always supply a photo. There's no fallback for a missing photo yet.

Checkbox.description: Lets the user turn one option on or off, or confirm something before continuing. state: unchecked (default), checked, error (acknowledging a destructive action). Properties: Label (text), ShowLabel (show or hide). The tick shows the checked state, so it doesn't rely on colour alone.

variantMatrix.note: The documentation frame (109:485) lays out state (rows: unchecked, checked) against ShowLabel (columns: True, False). The component set (117:23) publishes two variants, state=unchecked (117:12) and state=checked (117:15). Label (text, default "Label") and ShowLabel are component properties. The error state is named in the component description but is not drawn.

themes.note: The Checkbox frame renders every cell in one theme. It has no separate light and dark frames.

unboundValues.property: gap between the box and the label

use_when: To let the user opt in to something, such as marketing emails or staying signed in.
To confirm the user has read and agreed to terms before they continue, such as the booking terms or cancellation policy.
To make the user acknowledge a destructive action before it runs, using the error state (for example, "I understand this is permanent").
For a list of options where the user can choose any number, such as search filters.
dont_use_when: For a setting that takes effect immediately: use the Toggle component instead.
When the user must pick exactly one option from a list: use the Radiocard component instead.
To trigger an action: use the Button component instead.
best_practice: Always give the checkbox a visible label that says what ticking it does.
Write labels as positive statements ("Email me deals"), not negatives ("Don't email me").
Leave opt-in checkboxes unticked by default.
Make the whole label clickable, not just the 16px box.
Use the error state only for acknowledging destructive or irreversible actions.
Put extra detail in helper text below the label, not in the label itself.

Chip.description: A selectable pill for filtering results or switching category. state: unselected (default), selected (blue, a filter that's on), selected-strong (navy, the active category in a category row). Property: Label. One size, 32px high.

variantMatrix.note: The documentation frame (122:2) lays the three states out in one column, each beside a text label (unselected, selected, selected-strong). The component set (121:15) publishes three variants, state=unselected (121:8), state=selected (121:11) and state=selected-strong (121:13). Label (text, default "Label") is a component property, not a matrix axis. Every variant is 64x32 with the default label.

themes.note: The Chip frame renders every state once, in one theme. It has no separate light and dark frames.

use_when: To filter a list of results, such as search filters ("Pool", "Pet friendly", "Free cancellation").
To switch between categories of the same content, such as "All", "Bedrooms" or "Kitchen" in a photo gallery.
Use the selected state (blue) for filters the user has turned on, and selected-strong (navy) for the active category in a category row.
To show how many items an option holds, as part of the label (for example, "Kitchen 6").
dont_use_when: To show a status such as "Confirmed" or "Pending": use a Badge component instead.
To trigger an action, such as booking or submitting: use the Button component instead.
For a yes or no choice inside a form: use the Checkbox component instead.
To go to another page: use the Link component instead.
best_practice: Keep labels short: one to three words, plus an optional count.
A chip that's on must use a selected state, so the current selection is always visible.
Don't mix selected and selected-strong chips in the same row.
Space chips 8px apart in one row; let the row scroll or wrap on small screens rather than shrinking the chips.
When several filters can be on at once, give the user a way to clear them all.
Mark the selected chip for assistive technology (aria-pressed or aria-selected), not with colour alone.

Image.description: A photo in a fixed aspect ratio. ratio: 4:3 (default), 1:1, 3:2, 16:9, 2:1. radius: none (default; edge to edge inside a card), sm 6px (thumbnails), md 12px (standalone photos). The ratio is locked, so resize by width. Drop the photo onto the photo layer; it fills and crops to the frame.

variantMatrix.note: The documentation frame (124:2) lays out ratio (rows: 4:3, 1:1, 3:2, 16:9, 2:1) against radius (columns: none, sm, md). The component set (123:22) publishes all 15 variants, named ratio=4:3, radius=none through ratio=2:1, radius=md. Figma draws no states.

themes.note: The Image frame renders every cell in one theme. It has no separate light and dark frames.

use_when: To show a photo of a listing, room or place, such as the photo at the top of a property card or the photos in a listing gallery.
Use radius none for a photo that runs edge to edge inside a card; the card rounds the corners.
Use radius md (12px) for standalone photos such as the gallery and marketing tiles, and radius sm (6px) for small thumbnails in lists.
Use 16:9 for wide gallery and hero photos, 3:2 for property cards, 4:3 or 1:1 for thumbnails, and 2:1 for banners and marketing tiles.
dont_use_when: For a person's profile photo: use the Avatar component instead.
For the Horizon Stays brand mark: use the Logo component instead.
For icons or small symbols: use an icon from the Icon Library instead.
best_practice: Choose the ratio first, then resize by width; the ratio is locked, so photos never stretch.
Crop the photo to fill the frame; don't letterbox or distort it.
Keep one ratio and radius across a group, such as every card in a results list.
Give every meaningful image alt text that describes it; leave alt text empty for purely decorative images.
Show the placeholder while a photo loads, in the same ratio, so the layout doesn't jump.

Link.description: Text that takes the user to another page or runs a secondary action. size: md 13px (default), sm 12px (dense rows, beside filters). state: default, hover (underlined). Property: Label. Medium weight in color/text/link.

variantMatrix.note: The documentation frame (134:2) lays out state (rows: default, hover) against size (columns: md, sm). The component set (133:12) publishes all 4 variants, named size=md, state=default (133:4), size=md, state=hover (133:6), size=sm, state=default (133:8) and size=sm, state=hover (133:10). Label (text, default "Link") is a component property, not a matrix axis. Figma draws no focus, visited or disabled variants.

themes.note: The Link frame renders every cell once, in one theme. It has no separate light and dark frames.

use_when: To take the user to another page or view, such as "Show all 24 amenities" or "Forgot your password?".
For a secondary action next to a form, such as "Resend code" or "Use a different email address".
To edit or manage an item in a list, such as "Edit" or "Manage" in account settings.
Use size md (13px) next to body text and on its own, and size sm (12px) in dense rows, such as "Clear" beside filters.
dont_use_when: For the main action on a page, such as submitting a form or booking: use the Button component instead.
To filter results or switch categories: use the Chip component instead.
To open a list of options to choose from: use the Dropdown component instead.
best_practice: Write link text that says where it goes or what it does ("Show all 24 amenities"), never "click here".
Keep links short, usually one to five words.
Underline a link that sits inside a sentence of body text, so it doesn't rely on colour alone; standalone links can use the default style.
Use the same link text for the same destination everywhere.
Leave space or a separator between two links next to each other.
Make sure every link shows a visible keyboard focus style.

Logo.description: The Horizon Stays logo. type: lockup (default; mark and wordmark, the header logo), mark (the icon alone). 32px high, vector. Brand colours are fixed on purpose and don't follow UI tokens: mark #3B82F6 with white, wordmark #2e7cc4.

variantMatrix.note: The documentation frame (137:18) lays the two variants out in one column, each beside a text label. The component set (137:17) publishes two variants, type=lockup (137:6, 162x32) and type=mark (137:12, 32x32). Figma draws no states and no sizes.

themes.note: The Logo frame renders both variants once, in one theme, and has no separate light and dark frames. The mark is the committed SVG asset (src/assets/images/logo-mark.svg) with its colours fixed inside the file, and the wordmark colour is a fixed literal in the stylesheet, so neither follows the UI theme tokens and the Logo does not change between light and dark. Figma's Best Practice says there's no version for dark backgrounds yet.

unboundValues.property: fill colours inside the vector: tile #3B82F6, sun and wave white
unboundValues.codeNote: Set inside the SVG asset, not in the stylesheet

use_when: At the left of the header on every page, using the lockup at 32px high.
Use the mark on its own where there's no room for the wordmark, such as a collapsed sidebar, an app icon or a favicon.
dont_use_when: For listing, room or place photos: use the Image component instead.
For a person's profile photo: use the Avatar component instead.
As a decorative icon or bullet: use an icon from the Icon Library instead.
best_practice: Use the logo as it is: don't recolour, stretch, rotate or add effects to it.
Scale an instance proportionally only (hold Shift while resizing); never change its width and height separately.
Don't edit the wordmark text or retype it in another font.
Leave clear space around the logo; don't crowd it with other elements.
Place it on a light background so the blue stays readable; there's no version for dark backgrounds yet.
Don't show the mark and the lockup side by side on the same screen.

internal.name: _progressbar-bar
internal.description: Internal part of progressbar (not for direct use). value sets the fill length in steps of 10; the fill scales with the bar's width.

ProgressBar.description: Shows a value against a known total, such as occupancy or a share of revenue. size: md 8px (default), sm 6px (dense layouts such as calendar cells). tone: primary (default), success, neutral, inverse (on navy). value: 0 to 100 in steps of 10 (from the nested bar; default 60), then type the matching Value text. Properties: Label, Value, Helper, ShowLabel, ShowHelper.

variantMatrix.note: The component set (140:66) publishes all 8 variants, named size=md, tone=primary (140:5) through size=sm, tone=inverse (140:59). Label, Value, Helper, ShowLabel and ShowHelper are component properties, not matrix axes. The two tone=inverse cells (140:52, 140:59) are published in Figma but not built: see the design gap "ProgressBar inverse tone not built" below. Figma draws no states.

themes.note: The progressbar component set renders every cell once, in one theme. It has no separate light and dark frames.

use_when: To show how full something is against a known total, such as a property's occupancy for a night ("38 of 48 · 79%").
To compare parts of a whole side by side, such as revenue by booking channel, with each share as the Value.
To show a score out of a maximum, such as review scores by category; hide the label row when the layout already names it.
Use tone inverse on navy backgrounds, such as a sold-out night in the calendar.
dont_use_when: For steps in a flow, such as "1 of 3": use the Stepper component instead.
To compare exact figures across many rows: use the Table component instead.
best_practice: Always show the number too, as the Value or a nearby label; the bar alone isn't precise and screen readers can't read it.
Pick the value (0 to 100 in steps of 10) and type the same number in Value, so the bar and the text agree.
Keep bars in the same group the same size and width so they can be compared.
Give colours a consistent meaning, such as one colour per booking channel, and name it in the label.
Use size sm in dense layouts such as calendar cells, and md everywhere else.
Keep the fill between 0 and 100%; show overbooking with a separate marker, not a bar longer than its track.

Toggle.description: Turns a single setting on or off, and the change applies straight away. size: md 44x24 (default; settings lists), sm 40x22 (dense tables). state: off (default), on, disabled-off, disabled-on. No built-in label: place the setting's label beside it.

variantMatrix.note: The documentation frame (145:2) lays out size (rows: md, sm) against state (columns: off, on, disabled-off, disabled-on). The component set (144:20) publishes all 8 variants, named size=md, state=off (144:4) through size=sm, state=disabled-on (144:18). In Figma, state is one combined property.

themes.note: The toggle component set renders every cell once, in one theme. It has no separate light and dark frames.

use_when: To turn a single setting on or off, such as a notification ("Check in reminders", "Price drop alerts").
For a setting that takes effect immediately, without a Save button.
Use size md in settings lists, with the label and helper text on the left and the toggle on the right; use size sm in dense tables, such as the Email, Push and SMS columns.
Use a disabled state for a setting the user can't change, such as booking confirmations that are always sent.
dont_use_when: For a choice submitted together with a form, such as agreeing to terms: use the Checkbox component instead.
When the user must choose one of several options: use the Radiocard component instead.
To trigger an action, such as saving or sending: use the Button component instead.
best_practice: Always pair the toggle with a visible label that names the setting, not its state ("Price drop alerts", not "On").
Apply the change straight away; don't make the user press Save afterwards.
Leave optional notifications and marketing off by default.
Explain why a disabled toggle can't be changed in the helper text (for example, "Always on, cannot be changed").
Make the whole row clickable, not only the switch.
Give the toggle the switch role and its label for assistive technology (role="switch" with aria-checked).

Breadcrumbs.description: Shows where the current page sits in the site's hierarchy, above the page title. Ancestors are links in color/text/secondary that underline on hover; the current page is color/text/primary and not a link. Properties: Item 1, Item 2, Item 3, Current, ShowItem2 and ShowItem3 (2 to 4 levels). 12px.

variantMatrix.note: Breadcrumbs (163:2) is a single component with two boolean properties, ShowItem2 and ShowItem3, not a variant set. The documentation frame (163:13) draws the four combinations as 164:1504 (ShowItem2 true, ShowItem3 true), 164:1516 (ShowItem2 false, ShowItem3 true), 164:1529 (ShowItem2 true, ShowItem3 false) and 164:1542 (both false), and repeats two of them as the 3 levels row (163:16) and the 2 levels row (163:29). Item 1, Item 2, Item 3 and Current are text properties, not matrix axes. Figma draws no hover, focus or visited variants.

themes.note: The Breadcrumbs frame renders every cell once, in one theme. It has no separate light and dark frames.

use_when: Above the page title on pages that sit inside a hierarchy, such as a listing ("Stays / Portugal / Lisbon / Alfama") or a back office settings page ("Team and roles / Roles / Permissions").
To let the user go back up to any parent page in one click.
Show 2 to 4 levels; hide unused levels with ShowItem2 and ShowItem3.
dont_use_when: On top-level pages that have no parent: there's nothing to show.
To show the steps of a flow, such as checkout: use the Stepper component instead.
As the main navigation between sections: use the Sidebar or Header component instead.
best_practice: Make every item except the current page a link to that page.
Use the same page names as the page titles and navigation, so the trail is easy to recognise.
Keep the current page as the last item, styled darker and not as a link.
Don't wrap breadcrumbs onto two lines; shorten long names instead.
Mark the trail up as navigation for assistive technology (a nav landmark with aria-label="Breadcrumb", and aria-current="page" on the last item).

internal.name: _buttongroup-segment
internal.description: Internal part of buttongroup type=segmented (not for direct use). One option: state unselected or selected.

ButtonGroup.description: Two or three related buttons, or a segmented control. type: primary (filled + outline, default), destructive (error + outline), secondary (two outlines), segmented (2 to 4 options, one selected in navy, the rest outlined; row only). layout: row (default, main action on the left), stack (full width, main action on top; not for segmented). ShowThird adds a third button or segment; ShowFourth adds a fourth segment (segmented only). Edit each button's or segment's text, and which segment is selected, from the group's properties.

variantMatrix.note: The documentation frame (192:44) lays out type (rows: primary, destructive, secondary, segmented) against layout (columns: row, stack). The component set (191:123) publishes 7 variants, named type=primary, layout=row through type=segmented, layout=row. It has no type=segmented, layout=stack variant, so the grid is 4 x 2 = 8 but 7 are published. ShowThird and ShowFourth are boolean properties of the set, not cells; the page draws them as the Examples ShowThird: true (192:58) and ShowThird + ShowFourth: true (195:964). Figma draws no hover, pressed or disabled states.

themes.note: The buttongroup frame renders every cell once, in one theme. It has no separate light and dark frames.

use_when: At the end of a dialog or form, to pair the main action with a way out, such as "Publish review" and "Save as draft", or "Save role and access" and "Cancel".
Use type destructive when the main action deletes or cancels something, such as "Continue to cancel" and "Keep my booking".
Use type secondary for two actions of equal weight, such as "View" and "Modify" on a trip card.
Use layout stack on narrow screens such as the mobile app, with the main action on top.
Use type segmented to switch a view between 2 to 4 options, such as the time range "Last 24 hours / 7 days / 30 days / Custom range" on the back office dashboard. Exactly one segment is selected.
usage.dont_use_when_heading: Do not use a button group
dont_use_when: For a single action: use the Button component instead.
To filter a list by several values at once: use the Chip component instead. Segments pick exactly one option.
For more than three actions, or more than four segments: move the extras into a Dropdown component.
best_practice: Put the main action first: on the left in a row, on top in a stack.
Use at most one filled button per group; the others are outline.
Label buttons with what they do ("Delete account", "Keep my account"), not "Yes" and "No".
Keep the whole group together; don't split its buttons across the layout.
In a destructive group, make the safe choice easy to find and never the filled button.

internal.name: _dropdown-option
internal.description: Internal part of dropdown (not for direct use). One option in the open menu: state default or selected.

Dropdown.description: Lets people pick one value from a list. size: md (36px, default, forms and sort) or sm (30px, compact filter bars). state: closed (default), open (shows the menu with the selected option highlighted), disabled. Label sits above the field (ShowLabel to hide it); Value is the current choice. Options in the open menu are _dropdown-option instances: edit their text, and which one is selected, from the layers.

variantMatrix.note: The documentation frame (196:2097) lays out state (rows: closed, open, disabled) against size (columns: md, sm), each cell an instance. The component set (199:66) publishes all 6 variants, named size=md, state=closed (199:12) through size=sm, state=disabled (199:60). In Figma, state is one property of the set. ShowLabel and Label are properties of the set, not cells; the page draws them as the instances ShowLabel: false (200:17) and Label + Value (200:24). Figma draws no hover, pressed, error or keyboard-focus states.

themes.note: The dropdown component set renders every cell once, in one theme. It has no separate light and dark frames.

vertical padding (the code computes it from --spacing-md with calc(), not a px literal)
drop shadow (an effect not bound to a variable)

use_when: To pick one value from a list of five or more, such as the property filter "All properties" on the back office calendar, or "Who" in the activity log filters.
Use size md (36px) in forms and for the sort control on search results; use size sm (30px) in compact filter bars and table headers.
Show the label above the field in forms. Hide it (ShowLabel off) only when the value says what it is, such as "Sort: Price, low first".
dont_use_when: For two to four options that should stay visible: use Buttongroup type segmented, or Radiocard.
To pick several values at once: use Chip filters or Checkboxes instead.
For actions such as "Export" or "Delete": use Button, or a Buttongroup.
best_practice: Always show a value in the field: the current choice or a neutral default such as "All properties". Never leave it blank.
Order options in a way people expect: by frequency, by time, or alphabetically, and put "All" first.
Keep option text short enough for one line at the field's width.

File.description: Lets people add files and shows the files they added. type dropzone: the area to drop or browse for files; state default (dashed border) or dragover (blue, while a file is held over it). Title and Hint carry the call to action and the accepted types and size limit. type item: one added file, with a type badge, File name, a meta line and an action; state uploaded (meta = type · size, action Remove), uploading (meta + Progressbar, action Cancel) or error (red, meta = the reason). Width 400, stretch to fill the form.

variantMatrix.note: The component set (204:41) publishes 5 variants, not the 10 that type x state would give: dropzone has default and dragover; item has uploaded, uploading and error. The documentation frame lays them out as two rows (type dropzone, type item) against the state columns. Title and Hint (dropzone) and File name, file type badge and meta (item) are properties of the set, not cells; the page draws them as the instances Back office photos (204:65) and Image file (204:69). Figma draws no hover, pressed, disabled or keyboard-focus states.

themes.note: The file component set renders every cell once, in one theme. It has no separate light and dark frames.

use_when: Use type dropzone where people add files: attachments in messages and support requests, room photos and verification documents in the back office.
Use type item for each file once it is added, in a list under the drop zone, with its name, type and size.
Show state uploading with the progress while a file is sending, and state error with the reason when a file is refused.
dont_use_when: To show a document people download but never upload, such as a receipt or invoice: use a Link or a table row.
For a profile photo: use Avatar with its own upload action.
Do not hide the limits: never leave the Hint empty.
best_practice: Put the accepted types and the size limit in the Hint, such as "PDF, JPG or PNG · 10 MB each".
Say what went wrong and how to fix it in the error, such as "Too large: the limit is 10 MB".
Keep the whole drop zone clickable, so "browse" works without dragging, on touch screens too.

registryLink.note: The registry's Figma cell holds the canvas page (node-id 57-1645), not the component set 213:54.

SearchBar.description: Lets people search. type field (default): a search input with a magnifier; size md (36px, web and back office) or lg (44px, mobile app); state empty (Placeholder), focused (blue border) or filled (Value, with a clear × button). type stay: the website's stay search, with Where, Check in, Check out and Guests values and a nested Search Button. Field width 320, stretch to fill.

Figma draws no hover, pressed, disabled or error state.

use_when: Use type field to search within one list or page, such as "Search messages", "Search reviews" or the back office "Search" in the header.
Use size md (36px) on web and in the back office; use size lg (44px) in the mobile app for a bigger tap target.
Use type stay at the top of the website and search results to find a stay by place, dates and guests.
usage.dont_use_when_heading: Do not use a search bar
dont_use_when: To filter by fixed values such as status or property: use Chip filters or a Dropdown.
To type data into a form, such as a name or an address: use a text field.
More than one type stay on the same page.
best_practice: Say what is being searched in the placeholder: "Search messages", not just "Search", unless the page makes it obvious.
Show the clear (×) button as soon as there is text, and keep the typed value after the results load.
In type stay, always show a value in each part, such as the dates already chosen, never an empty slot.

RadioCard.description: One option in a group where people pick exactly one, with room for a line of detail. state: unselected (default), selected (blue border and filled radio), disabled (greyed out, can't be picked). Title, Description (ShowDescription) and an optional Trailing text for a price (ShowTrailing). Width 480, stretch to fill; stack cards with 8px between them.

The documentation frame (212:22) draws only the three variants, one per state, and a "Payment group" of three instances (212:27, 212:35, 212:42). Figma draws no hover, pressed or focus state.

use_when: To pick one option from two to five where each needs a line of detail, such as the rate ("Whole apartment · non refundable"), when to pay, or which saved card to use at checkout.
Use the trailing text for the price of each option, such as "484.00 EUR" or "0.00 EUR now"; turn it off when options have no price, such as payment methods.
Use state disabled for an option that exists but can't be picked right now, such as a sold-out rate, and say why in the description.
usage.dont_use_when_heading: Do not use a radio card
dont_use_when: For more than five options, or options with no detail: use a Dropdown.
To pick several options: use Checkboxes.
To switch a view, such as a time range: use Buttongroup type segmented.
best_practice: Always preselect one card, usually the recommended or the current choice, such as the default card.
Stack cards vertically with 8px between them, all the same width, and make the whole card clickable.
Keep the title short and put conditions in the description, such as "free cancellation until 12 Sep".

Use type app at the top of each app screen below the status bar: back on the left, the screen name in the centre, one text action on the right when the screen has one, such as "Save" or "Mark read".
Use type backoffice above the content of each back office page, next to the Sidebar, with the page name and search.
dont_use_when: More than once on a page, or inside a card or a modal.
To hold page actions such as "Export" or "Add rate": put them in the page content, under the title.

best_practice: Keep the app title short (one or two words) so it stays centred and never truncates.
Turn ShowAvatar off for signed-out guests on web; the Book now button stays.
Hide the back chevron (ShowBack off) only on the top-level tabs of the app, such as Explore or Trips.

use_when: Use type progress at the top of a flow with three to five steps, such as booking: Dates and guests, Your details, Extras, Payment, Confirm.
Use type quantity to set a small number with − and +, such as Adults, Children and Rooms in the guests picker and filters.
Use state at-min when the value is at its lowest (0 children, 1 adult) and at-max at its highest, so the button can't go further.
dont_use_when: For a flow of one or two steps: a page title is enough.
For a number that can be large or exact, such as a price: use a text field.
To show how far something has loaded: use Progressbar.
best_practice: Keep step labels to one to three words, and let people go back to a done step by clicking it.
Mark every step before the current one as done; never skip ahead past an upcoming step.
Give each counter a clear label, and say the limits nearby when they aren't obvious, such as "Up to 8 guests".

Use type occupancy in the back office to see how full each day of a month is: rooms sold, the percentage, and sold-out days in navy.
Mark a stay with start and end on the check in and check out days, and in-range on the nights between.
dont_use_when: For a single known date such as a date of birth: use a date field.
To pick a time range for a report, such as the last 7 days: use Buttongroup type segmented.
To list bookings or events by day: use a Table.
best_practice: Grey out past days and strike through days that can't be booked, so people never pick a date that fails later.
Keep the price short with no currency on each day, and show the currency once nearby.
In occupancy, explain the colours under the grid, such as "Navy is sold out. Red percentages are above 95%."

use_when: Use type listing for something people can open or book: a stay, an experience, or a trip, with a photo, a title, one details line and the price.
Turn on ShowTag for a status on the photo, such as "Confirmed", and ShowAction for a text action such as "View"; turn ShowRating off when there are no reviews yet.
Use type stat in the back office for one key number, such as "Active admins 27", in a row of 3 to 5 tiles at the top of a page.
dont_use_when: For rows of data people compare or sort: use a Table.
To choose one option in a form: use Radiocard.
For a stat that needs a chart or several numbers: use a content panel, not a stat tile.
best_practice: Keep every card in a grid the same width and photo ratio, so titles and prices line up.
One line each for title and details: they cut off with … rather than wrap.
Make the whole listing card clickable, and keep the Action for a second, smaller step.

use_when: Use type section for a form inside a page, such as Profile, payment details or back office settings, with a Save changes and Cancel group at the end.
Use type card for a short form on its own, such as Sign in, Create your account or Invite someone, with one full-width button.
Build every input from textfield; use Dropdown, Checkbox, Radiocard or Toggle in the same stack when a field is a choice.
dont_use_when: For one setting that applies at once: use a Toggle, without a Save button.
To search or filter a list: use Searchbar or Chip filters.
For a long flow such as booking: split it into steps with Stepper type progress.
best_practice: Label every field above the input, and keep placeholders for examples, never for the label.
Show an error under the field that caused it and say how to fix it, such as "Use a full email address"; keep what the person typed.
Ask only for what you need, in the order people think about it, and put the main action last.

Title and Message, close × (ShowClose), a Content slot with detail rows you can replace with any content (ShowContent), the actions, and a Note (ShowNote). Place it on a color/bg/overlay backdrop.

ShowClose, ShowContent and ShowNote are boolean properties of the set, not variants; the documentation frame (233:12212) lays out 32 instances of them (2 types x 2 tones x ShowClose x ShowContent x ShowNote). The canvas also holds the example 'dialog on overlay' (244:74, 960x560, a 520 wide dialog on the color/bg/overlay rectangle) and one instance with ShowContent off (244:105). use_when: Use type dialog to confirm an action before it happens, such as "Remove Luis Correia?", or for a short task that must finish before going back, such as an invite.
Use tone destructive when the action deletes or can't be undone; show what changes in the content rows, such as "Can be undone: No".
Use type sheet on mobile for filters, pickers and short choices that slide up from the bottom.
dont_use_when: For information people should read while they keep working: show it on the page, or in a toast.
For long forms or anything with more than one step: use a page with Stepper.
Open a modal from another modal.
best_practice: Ask a question in the title and name the thing, such as "Remove Luis Correia?", and put the result of the action on the main button, such as "Remove admin", not "OK".
Always give a way out: Cancel, the close ×, the Escape key and a click on the backdrop.
Place the dialog in the centre on a color/bg/overlay backdrop; place the sheet at the bottom, full width.
